summary:
**Conversation overview**

The person is building a 3D model gallery/store in the GitHub repository 1998x-stack/3D-worlds (initially empty), wanting a well-organized, extensible file architecture using three.js as the core technology. They asked Claude to research three.js build frameworks and workflows in depth, create modeling SKILLs in .codex/skills, .pi/skills, and .claude/skills, build five models (table, chair, toilet, man, woman) using three.js, and design a professional, trustworthy GitHub Pages website where clicking each model shows an enlarged view with a copy button allowing users to directly import the model into their own projects. They also requested a SQLite model database (anticipating tens of thousands of models eventually) and a deliverable MCP server so users building 3D games could import models through it, with careful schema and system design for extensibility.

Claude noted it could not directly push to the GitHub repository since the GitHub account wasn't connected to the session, so it planned to build the full repository locally and deliver it as a compressed archive with push instructions, with direct push available once GitHub is connected. Claude broke the work into a task list: researching three.js (versions, WebGPURenderer/TSL status, GLTFExporter in Node, GitHub Pages workflows, MCP SDK, SKILL conventions), writing design docs, building the five models, a catalog-building tool (GLTFExporter + gltf-validator + SQLite), the gallery website (Vite + three.js), the MCP service (search_models, get_model, list_categories, import_model, get_import_snippet), SKILL files synced across the three directories, CI/Pages configuration, verification, and final packaging. Claude recorded project details in memory and began technical research via web search/fetch and local environment checks (Node, npm package versions, Chrome, SQLite with FTS5/JSON support).
